cases.input: An IVDR serious-incident/FSCA case has a completed investigation, reconciled FSCA execution and effectiveness evidence, no material new safety facts, and verified current MIR/FSCA reporting requirements. Prepare the manufacturer final/follow-up package and authority-state handoff.
requiredBehaviors: verify current report form schema channel and authority context before final package creation
build a versioned final package from existing investigation risk FSCA and effectiveness evidence without recomputing execution effectiveness
separate manufacturer final submission authority receipt review and authority closure states
forbiddenBehaviors: use an obsolete reporting form without current-source verification
treat the manufacturer final report as competent-authority closure
create a second independent FSCA effectiveness assessment
skillAnchors: FSCA execution evidence is consumed, not recomputed

cases.input: The operational FSCA is nearly complete, but root cause remains unresolved and management wants to file a Final (Non-reportable) incident to close the case administratively.
requiredBehaviors: keep unresolved root cause or contributing-factor uncertainty explicit in final-report readiness
block a Final Non-reportable shortcut when the required causal basis is not established
keep the case in an appropriate open follow-up or investigation state while preserving completed FSCA evidence
forbiddenBehaviors: use a Final Non-reportable label to bypass unresolved causality
rewrite completed FSCA execution evidence as incomplete merely because investigation remains open
infer competent-authority acceptance from lack of questions

cases.input: A final package is approved internally when a corrected device causes a new serious incident in a newly affected country and another lot is implicated. The team wants to submit the approved package unchanged and address the new facts later.
requiredBehaviors: interrupt finalization and preserve the approved package version as historical rather than submitting it unchanged
route the new serious incident and additional lot to vigilance FSCA risk CAPA and scope reassessment immediately
create a new market and scope version that includes the newly affected country before subsequent reporting
forbiddenBehaviors: submit a superseded final package after material new safety and scope evidence
delay vigilance reassessment until after administrative finalization
hide the newly affected country or lot outside the controlled scope history

cases.input: After a manufacturer final report is submitted, the evaluating authority asks for more evidence and the notified body separately asks for a CAPA update. No authority has issued a closure decision. Management wants one combined closed state.
requiredBehaviors: record competent-authority and notified-body requests as separate append-only external events
create controlled follow-up response versions while preserving the submitted final report
keep authority-review-pending or more-information-required until verified competent-authority closure evidence exists
forbiddenBehaviors: collapse notified-body and competent-authority states into one closed state
overwrite the submitted manufacturer final report with later authority feedback
infer authority closure from submission or silence
skillAnchors: Notified Body and Authority states stay distinct
